text:
Recommended instrumentation: record original tokens, selected positions, corruption branch, corrupted input and loss weights. Assert each selected label equals the original token at that position; unselected/padding positions contribute no loss. Force MASK/random/unchanged branches separately: BERT’s 80/10/10 policy permits selected inputs to equal targets, including random replacements matching originals. Repeated item IDs require position-based provenance; target IDs elsewhere in history are legitimate. Include a deliberately shifted-label fixture that must fail. These checks follow [BERT’s masking implementation](https://github.com/google-research/bert/blob/master/create_pretraining_data.py).

For bidirectionality, inspect effective attention masks and perturb a valid token right of an interior query: a controlled nondegenerate attention fixture must transmit that change. Perturb padding embeddings while keeping positions and padding masks fixed: valid outputs must remain unchanged; perturbing an allowed token supplies an independent positive control. Exclude padding from attention keys, target selection and loss. For left-padded inference, independently construct truncated-history-plus-MASK fixtures, including repeated IDs and maximum-length histories; assert readout uses the appended MASK’s absolute index, never nonpadding-count minus one. [RecTools documents padding-only attention and appended-MASK inference](https://rectools.readthedocs.io/en/stable/examples/tutorials/transformers_tutorial.html).

Reload each category’s single checkpoint through the generated predictor in a fresh process; verify configuration, item mapping, preprocessing, candidate scores and ordering against the in-memory model using independently specified fixtures. Use eval mode and inference mode. Require exact IDs/masks; compare finite float32 scores with explicit tolerances, initially PyTorch’s rtol=1.3e-6, atol=1e-5. Log maximum errors; investigate near-tie ranking differences rather than silently widening tolerances. [PyTorch specifies these defaults](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/testing.html). Integration estimate: small fixtures, hooks and one reload per category; low runtime overhead without retraining, with implementation effort depending on sampler/predictor separation.
